summary: You need 135 graduate units, including 70 letter-graded units of graduate coursework: ENGLISH 396, one 5-unit course in each of the four areas (pre-1700, post-1700, theory or methodology, and a literature outside your geographical focus), and other graded 200-level English courses, with at most 5 units each of ENGLISH 398 and 398R. You also take ENGLISH 396L, 398Q and six quarters of 398W, and at least six letter-graded 300-level seminars, which independent study, research and thesis units do not count toward; at most 10 units at the 100 level count. Area courses not on the lists and outside-department courses the Director of Graduate Studies approves are moved in by hand. The language requirement can be met by a reading exam, a B or better in a 250 reading course or a foreign literature course, or an approved certificate, and teaching, candidacy, the general and oral exams and the dissertation are recorded by the department.

totals.why: "Students may count no more than ten 100-level units towards the 65 units at the discretion of the Director of Graduate Studies." The 70 graded units are graduate level ("courses numbered 200 or higher"), so this caps 100-level units in the program.

ENGLISH 396 moves to the 70 graded units ("The 70 graded units must include ENGLISH 396"). "ENGLISH 398W, the cohort seminar course, is to be taken in spring quarter of the second year; autumn, winter, and spring of the third year; and autumn and winter of the fourth year": six enrollments.

add.why: "Of all courses taken, a minimum of six courses for a letter grade must be 300-level graduate seminars." A designation over courses counted elsewhere. The required non-graded courses (396L, 398Q, 398W, and 398A), which the catalog offers only as S/NC, are left out, and so are ENGLISH 394 Independent Study, ENGLISH 398 Research Course and ENGLISH 399 Thesis, which are not seminars ("Research units are taken under ENGLISH 398 with the Introductory Advisor or their program advisor").
